name: Randomized trial risk of bias (RoB 2 structure)
description: Records reviewer judgments for a randomized trial across the five RoB 2 domains. Answers produce an advisory suggestion for each domain and overall; the reviewer makes the final call and explains any change.

applicability.note: Domains follow the structure of Cochrane RoB 2 (Sterne et al., BMJ 2019). Question wording is DeepRef's own; consult the official RoB 2 guidance for full criteria.

domains.label: Bias arising from the randomization process
domains.description: Whether the allocation sequence was unpredictable, whether enrolment staff could foresee assignments, and whether the arms were comparable at baseline.

questions.label: Was the allocation sequence generated by a chance-based method, such as computer random numbers or a random-number table?
questions.help: Predictable schemes such as alternation, record or birth order, or dates do not count. Answer no information if the report does not say how the sequence was made.

questions.label: Were the people who enrolled participants unable to foresee the next assignment until enrolment was final?
questions.help: Central or remote allocation, pharmacy-controlled supplies and numbered sealed containers count. Open allocation lists do not.

questions.label: Were the arms comparable at baseline, with no imbalance that suggests the randomization itself went wrong?
questions.help: Check the baseline table. Small chance differences on their own do not indicate a problem.

domains.label: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domains.description: Whether participants and staff knew their assignment, whether departures from the plan were unbalanced or influential, and whether the analysis reflected the randomized groups.

questions.label: Were participants and the staff delivering the intervention unaware of which arm each person was in?
questions.help: Answer no if blinding was not possible or not used, and note the reason in the rationale.

questions.label: Did departures from the planned intervention, such as crossover, co-interventions or poor adherence, differ between arms or plausibly change the outcome?
questions.help: Yes means the departures were unbalanced or influential. Answer no if they were rare or spread evenly across arms.

questions.label: Was the primary outcome analysed by assigned arm, including all randomized participants, or with an equivalent approach?
questions.help: Analyses limited to adherent participants, or that drop participants without justification, do not count.

questions.label: If an effect of actually receiving or adhering to the intervention was reported, was the analysis suited to that question?
questions.help: Answer not applicable when the report gives no such effect estimate.

domains.label: Bias due to missing outcome data
domains.description: Whether outcome data were nearly complete and whether any missing data could be linked to the outcome.

questions.label: Were outcome data obtained for nearly all randomized participants?
questions.help: Compare the number analysed with the number randomized in each arm.

questions.label: Is there reason to think the missing outcome data were linked to the true outcome, for example through different dropout between arms or dropout among people doing worse?
questions.help: Yes means such a link is plausible. Answer no information if the report does not say why data were missing.

questions.label: Was any missing outcome data handled with a justified method, such as a sensitivity analysis or a reasoned imputation?
questions.help: Answer not applicable if the outcome data were complete.

domains.label: Bias in measurement of the outcome
domains.description: Whether outcome measurement was equivalent across arms and, where the outcome is subjective, whether assessors were kept unaware of the arm.

questions.label: Were the outcome measurement method, instrument and timing the same in every arm?
questions.help: Differences in how the outcome was collected between arms can bias the comparison.

questions.label: Were the people assessing the outcome unaware of each participant's arm?
questions.help: Answer not applicable if the outcome is objective (for example death or a laboratory value), so assessor knowledge could not change it.

domains.label: Bias in selection of the reported result
domains.description: Whether the analysis was planned before results were known and whether the reported result appears to have been chosen from several options.

questions.label: Was this outcome and analysis specified in a protocol, registry entry or analysis plan dated before results were available?
questions.help: Answer no information if no registration or protocol is cited.

questions.label: Were several outcome measures, time points or analyses available, with the reported one chosen from among them?
questions.help: Yes means the reported result was one of several options. Answer no if a single primary outcome and analysis were specified.

questions.label: Is there any sign that the reported result was chosen because it was statistically significant or more favourable?
questions.help: Look for outcomes or subgroups that appear only in the report, or a primary outcome that changed from the protocol.
